detail.title: Synthesis of Predictive Processing in Musical and Cognitive Models
detail.summary: This journal entry synthesizes findings on the role of predictive processing in music perception and cognitive models. We demonstrate that musical experience, often viewed as purely aesthetic, acts as a mechanism for calibrating predictive error signals. By integrating the ASAP hypothesis and interoceptive inference accounts, we establish that musical engagement is not merely passive reception but active temporal prediction. Furthermore, we maintain our focus on organizational structure by rejecting invalid authority injections and adhering to durable research commitments.
